entities.name: PMID:27515540
observations: Tièche, da Costa, and Streit; BMC Health Services Research 2016;16:373; DOI 10.1186/s12913-016-1647-4.
Single Swiss primary-care practice; pretest-posttest comparison with 153 patients before and 153 after renovation.
Questionnaire assessed office appearance, medical assistants, general practitioners, and overall satisfaction using 12 six-point Likert indicators.
Post-renovation ratings were higher in all four domains, with reported significance from p<0.01 to p<0.001; adjusted analyses remained significant at p<0.01.
Authors interpreted higher ratings in unchanged care-related domains as contextual/perceptual bias caused by the renovated interior.

entities.name: Renovation satisfaction bias
observations: In a pretest-posttest study of one primary-care office, interior renovation was followed by significantly higher patient ratings across office, staff, physician, and overall satisfaction domains.
Because ratings increased even for domains not directly renovated, the authors concluded that the interior environment biased perceptions of care quality.

source_tools.relevance: Main causal interpretation reported by the study authors.
